She wears a fitted black cropped tactical top with the front zip pulled low to show cleavage and a bare toned midriff; over it her white-and-gold guild medic jacket, cropped short and worn open, the guild crest on the right shoulder, the left sleeve torn away and the jacket slipping off that bare shoulder and arm; fitted low-rise black cargo trousers with a utility belt and a cracked tablet clipped at her hip. Streaks of grey ash on the white jacket, green screen light on her glossy hair. Waist-up in the lower part of the picture, three-quarter view, eye level, one hand on her hip and the other raised, swiping a small floating interface panel; looking at the viewer with a sly smirk, dry and clinical, as if she has already done the arithmetic. Colour palette: green-black, acid green, hot magenta and white; acid green dominates, not blue or cyan. She is the only person in the picture, clearly a grown woman, dressed in opaque fabric. The interface panels show only bars and icons: nothing written anywhere, no text, no letters, no logo.
